# Renewable Energy Provision

Renewable energy provision values the electricity a country generates from wind, sun and
geothermal heat, and attributes to nature the part of that value the resource itself provided
rather than the turbines, panels and grid that capture it. The base year is 2019. Solar, wind and
geothermal are three rows of the account, computed in this one module.

## Source

The write-up is `Renewable_Energy_Provisions.docx` in the shared folder of current write-ups
(version of 28 October 2026). The registered author code is
`jacob-harr/gep_renewable_energy_production` at `cead3eb` (6 October 2026). The library does not
port that revision's share, as the section on the rent share explains.

## Data and Methods

Three resources are valued separately and summed: wind, solar and geothermal. For each, IRENA
reports the electricity a country generated, in gigawatt hours. IRENA splits each resource across
sub-technologies and producer types, which are summed to one figure per country, resource and
year.

That generation is priced at the World Bank electricity price series, which arrives in US cents
per kilowatt-hour and is converted to dollars per gigawatt hour.

$$
\text{GEP}_{\text{renewable}} = \sum_{c,r} \text{Generation}_{c,r} \cdot \text{Price}_{c}
\cdot \lambda_{c}
$$

for country $c$ and resource $r$.

## The rent share

Generation times price is revenue, and most of that revenue pays for the equipment, the
maintenance and the grid. The part attributable to the resource is what economists call the
resource rent: what is left after every other factor of production has been paid. A wind farm's
rent is what the wind contributes, once the turbines and the operators have been covered.

$\lambda_c$ is that share, computed by the module author with the Changing Wealth of Nations
HYDROPOWER rent method (rent over revenue per country-year) and applied to all three
technologies as a proxy, joined on country name and year. It is the same idea as the land rental
rate crop provision uses, applied to an energy resource instead of to land.

A country can come out at zero or below. That comes from the rent attribution, not from
generation, so it is a country whose renewable generation earned no rent that year rather than a
country that generated nothing. Those rows are dropped.

## Validation

A fresh run on the cached inputs reproduces the saved tables: the 28 October 2026 regeneration
left every valued country and all three per-technology tables byte-identical, changing only the
combined table's fabricated zeros to missing. Three vintages of per-technology tables now exist
and no two agree. The author repository's current outputs (revision cead3eb) carry the
normalized-capacity-factor lambda: $193.2bn over 183 countries against this module's $173.5bn
over 143, overlap correlations 0.90–0.93 per technology, every country this module values also
valued there. The reference_outputs staged in base_data match neither (solar $80.0bn over 172,
wind $45.6bn over 121, geothermal $9.0bn over 26). Which revision produced them is not
determined. Which construction the account adopts is the open question below.

## What is open

The October meeting rejected the borrowed hydropower share and asked the author for supported
resource rents, with explicit treatment of operating and capital costs (decision M10). The
author's current code and write-up instead derive $\lambda$ from a per-technology normalised
capacity factor, a third construction. The write-up does not state how a capacity factor maps to
a rent share, and the document's own review comments question the premise. The supplied inputs
carry no operating or capital costs, so a resource rent cannot yet be computed from them. Steve
reviews the nature share in the tracker. Jacob was asked on 28 October, and the follow-up is held
for that review. This module's numbers stay as they are until the share is decided.

## References

1. IRENA (2023). *Renewable Energy Statistics*. International Renewable Energy Agency.
2. World Bank (2024). *The Changing Wealth of Nations: Revisiting the Measurement of
   Comprehensive Wealth*.

## Coverage

The published combined table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019,
in 2019 USD. 143 carry a value, totalling \$173,493,644,889.46, and 107 have no retained positive
estimate. The valuation keeps positive values only. The 2019 check found 48 negative technology
rows dropped (23 solar, 20 wind, 5 geothermal), so a missing row does not say whether the inputs
were absent or an estimate was computed and excluded. The table holds no zeros.

The three technology tables list only their valued countries: solar 142 (\$54,410,978,171.74),
wind 98 (\$112,524,374,333.31) and geothermal 21 (\$6,558,292,384.42).
